rationale:
The quota for 2026-11-28 is 1 long video, 3 Shorts and 0 carousels.

**Long video.** Most of the playbook queue is already done:
- #1 Foundayo What to Expect is live (ssb7Zcs3KSY).
- #2 Mounjaro vs Ozempic has been live since 11-23.
- #5 Vial vs Pen is live (LH-HTtwKz5I).
- #3 Serious Risks has been re-timed and must not be scripted again.

That leaves #4, "Tirzepatide After 6 Months" (series part 3, open until 11-30). It was held on 11-25 with a known fix list, and the radar shows it at a steady momentum of 80. It is a what-to-expect timeline, which is a search-demand format. It rests only on the label and SURMOUNT-1 to 72 weeks, so it is settled evidence that can be checked in depth. The playbook explicitly allows re-rendering a held video, and that is the lowest-risk way to make sure a long video ships today. Two of the last 7 long videos were already search-demand formats (Vial vs Pen, After 6 Months), so the long slot didn't have to be one; this pick is one anyway, and it extends the First Month → Months 2–6 series. If the render is held again, ship the re-timed Serious Risks the same day.

I turned down the other long candidates:
- **NAION:** peaking fast-moving news, and there's already an 11-10 Short.
- **Cancer umbrella review:** fresh and not settled enough to fact-check in depth.
- **Type 1 diabetes, mammograms, Wegovy pill comparison, retatrutide:** caution items, or pipeline drugs, or outside the 48-hour fast-turn window.
- **Muscle and stopping/regain:** too close to the live Strength, Protein, Stopping and Keeping Results videos.

**Shorts.** From today the slots go back to body, pen and approved-drug felt-symptom moments, so every Short is a felt moment with the drug named first:
- **S1, 08:00:** heartburn when lying down at night. This is a different angle from the 11-10 holiday-meal heartburn Short.
- **S2, 13:00:** Foundayo constipation. It pairs a searched approved-drug name with a felt symptom, the format behind Foundayo nausea's 857 views, and it hasn't been covered.
- **S3, 20:00:** lower readings on a home blood-pressure cuff, as a spin-off of L1. It carries the firm line about never changing blood pressure medicines on your own.

I skipped the radar's hair, pen-blood, injection-site and morning-after nausea angles because we covered them within the last 30 days. The Christmas Shorts are held for mid-December, closer to the peak.

**Mix.** Pillars rotate across results, get-the-most, life-on-glp1 and beyond-weight, with no pillar used more than once. Body systems are varied: 2 digestive, 1 heart and circulation. There is 1 rising-trend Short (Foundayo search) and the rest are evergreen with a timely hook. S3 has a myth-busting edge ("lower readings don't mean adjust it yourself").

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) after 6 months: what to expect from month 6 onward (the rest of the SURMOUNT-1 average curve to 72 weeks, side effects easing per the label, waist and blood pressure changes at 72 weeks, the 3-year prediabetes follow-up, and the shift toward keeping muscle and results). Series part 3. This re-renders the held 11-25 script; don't write a new script.

Sentence 1 answers the title in its own words: average loss kept going but slowed, and the focus shifts to keeping results. No new facts after 80%, no 'now' or 'new', and no dose numbers.

Before publishing, check the live list for duplicates: this must not repeat Plateau, How Long or Months 2–6.

Render ship-blockers: every cut within 0.5 s of its beat, masking 0.02 or lower, a word-for-word transcript, and a description ending '…whether it's right for you.'

Watch-next target: Keeping Results.

pieces.topic: Heartburn when you lie down at night on tirzepatide: what the label reports, and the NHS bedtime reflux habits
pieces.angle: Sentence 1: 'Heartburn when you lie down on tirzepatide? Reflux is a listed, common side effect.' (14 words). Sentence 2 card: 'Reflux (GERD): 5% on tirzepatide 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, pooled weight trials in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes.' An optional separate sentence can give indigestion at 10% vs 4%. Then the separate label sentence 'Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying.' with no 'so'. NHS habits, tagged NHS: 'Do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed.' and 'Raise the head of your bed by around 10 to 20 cm, so your chest and head are above your waist.' Untagged: ask a pharmacist before any antacid. Untagged: see your doctor if food gets stuck, you vomit often or you lose weight without trying. Chest pain, vomiting blood or black stools mean your local urgent care or emergency number. Close with the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Post note target: Side Effects.
pieces.why: A felt-symptom 'Is this normal?' moment for the morning slot. The bedtime angle is different from the 11-10 holiday-meal heartburn Short, and it feeds Side Effects, our top suggested-traffic earner. | fact-check: Checked. The Zepbound label's Table 2 (pooled Study 1 and Study 2, adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes) lists gastroesophageal reflux disease at 5% on 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, and dyspepsia at 10% on 15 mg vs 4% on placebo. The label sentence is "ZEPBOUND delays gastric emptying and thereby has the potential to impact the absorption of concomitantly administered oral medications." Use it only as the separate sentence 'Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying', with no causal link to heartburn. NHS wording checked: "do not eat within 3 or 4 hours before bed" and "raising the head of your bed by around 10 to 20cm, so your chest and head are above your waist, helps relieve symptoms." Fixes: (1) The label never says 'heartburn' or 'when you lie down', so sentence 1 must not suggest it does. Name the label terms. (2) Use one number per sentence and keep the pooled population on the card. (3) Add the NHS see-a-GP signs to the untagged urgent line: food getting stuck, frequent vomiting, unexplained weight loss. Keep chest pain, vomiting blood and black stools as emergency signs. (4) Cite the printed date of the exact label document you link. The HTML label shows 'Revised: 8/2026'.

pieces.topic: Backed up on Foundayo (orforglipron)? Constipation on the US label's common list, and gentle fluid and fibre habits
pieces.angle: Sentence 1: 'Foundayo, the orforglipron pill, and feeling backed up? Constipation is a common, listed side effect.' Card: 'Constipation (adverse reaction): 24% on Foundayo 17.2 mg vs 9% on placebo, pooled Trials 1 and 2: adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes.' Untagged tips: build fibre up gradually with fluids, unless you've been told to limit fluids, and take a gentle walk. Ask a pharmacist before any laxative, with no product names. Untagged: if constipation is severe or keeps getting worse, contact your prescriber. Then the Foundayo emergency card with the full guide wording ('severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting … right away'), the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line.
pieces.why: Pairs a searched approved-drug name with a felt symptom, the format behind Foundayo nausea (857) and food rules (1,063). It hasn't been covered, and it feeds the new Foundayo long video, which has a 71% average view. | fact-check: Checked. The Foundayo label prints constipation in the pooled placebo-controlled ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 table: 20% (5.5 mg), 27% (9 mg) and 24% (17.2 mg, the top label dose) vs 9% on placebo. Constipation is one of the label's most common adverse reactions. The rate goes on the card as 24% vs 9%. Never say 'up to 24%', because 9 mg was higher at 27%. Use 'adverse reactions', never 'side effects', on the rate card. The label's postmarketing section reports severe constipation, including fecal impaction. Add an untagged line pointing people with severe or worsening constipation to their prescriber, but don't present it as a common outcome. Fibre, fluid and walking tips are our own: no source tag, and never placed straight after a label claim. Keep the Foundayo pancreatitis wording 'with or without nausea or vomiting'. Cite 'Revised: 7/2026' only if that date is printed on the exact document linked. Watch-next target: ssb7Zcs3KSY.

pieces.topic: Home blood pressure readings lower months into tirzepatide: what SURMOUNT-1 reported at 72 weeks, and why you never change blood pressure medicines on your own
pieces.angle: Sentence 1: 'Home blood pressure cuff reading lower on tirzepatide? Bring those numbers to your doctor.' Sentence 2 card: in SURMOUNT-1, average systolic blood pressure fell more on tirzepatide than on placebo at 72 weeks, using the exact NEJM mmHg figures for both groups, in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Label line: 'Among people taking tirzepatide, low blood pressure was reported more often in those also on blood pressure medicines: 2.2% vs 1.2%.' Firm untagged line: never change blood pressure medicines on your own, and review lower readings and any dizziness with your doctor. Untagged: fainting, chest pain or confusion mean your local emergency number. Close with the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Post note target: L1 once it's verified live, otherwise Side Effects.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide: Blood Pressure Reading Lower at Home? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1 (After 6 Months covers 72-week blood pressure changes) that drives traffic to the long video. It's a felt home-monitor moment with a contrarian-but-true point: lower readings don't mean adjusting your medicines yourself. | fact-check: Fits the channel and the guardrails: it says outright never to change blood pressure medicines on your own. Checked the label line. The Zepbound label says: "Hypotension was more frequently seen in ZEPBOUND-treated patients on concomitant antihypertensive therapy (2.2%) compared to ZEPBOUND-treated patients not on antihypertensive therapy (1.2%)." This compares tirzepatide users with each other, not tirzepatide with placebo. The card must say so and must not imply a placebo comparison. The SURMOUNT-1 systolic figures must be copied exactly from L1's verified script and NEJM: mean change at 72 weeks, tirzepatide vs placebo, full population, in mmHg. Don't publish S3 ahead of a verified L1 unless the figures were checked on their own. Never imply that lower readings mean you can cut back on medicine. Fix the source date (the HTML label prints 'Revised: 8/2026').
